intro: The body in detail, what it does on its own, and the verbs for postures and gestures.
p.frente.consejo: There is also «frente a», meaning «in front of»: «frente a la puerta».
p.mejilla.consejo: In Spain people greet with two kisses: one on each «mejilla».
p.barbilla.consejo: A slightly more technical synonym is «mentón».
p.ceja.consejo: When surprised, people «levantan las cejas» (raise their eyebrows).
p.pestaña.consejo: From it comes «pestañear»: opening and closing the eyes very fast.
p.arruga.consejo: There are also «arrugas» in badly folded clothes.
p.agacharse.consejo: It is the movement: «me agaché». If you are already down, you are «agachado».
p.tumbarse.consejo: It is the movement: «me tumbé». The result is «estar tumbado».
p.quedarse quieto.consejo: It agrees with who stays: «ella se queda quieta», «ellos se quedan quietos».
p.bostezar.consejo: Before «e» the z becomes c: «bosteza», but «bostece».
p.estornudar.consejo: When someone sneezes, in Spain people say «¡Salud!».
p.sudar.consejo: From «sudar» comes «el sudor». «Sudar la gota gorda» means to make a great effort.
p.rascarse.consejo: With the body you use the article: «se rasca la cabeza».
p.acariciar.consejo: With people and animals it takes «a»: «acaricia a un gato».
b1.texto:
**The face.** **La frente**, **las cejas**, **las pestañas**, **las mejillas** and **la barbilla**. With age come **arrugas** and **canas**.

**Postures: movement or result.** Spanish keeps the two apart:

- Movement, with a reflexive verb: **me agaché**, **se tumbó**, **se sentó**.
- Result, with **estar** or **quedarse**: **estaba agachado**, **estaba tumbada**, **me quedé quieto**.

**What the body does on its own:** **bostezar**, **estornudar**, **sudar**.

**With the hands:** **acariciar** a cat, **rascarse** the head, **señalar** with a finger.

With the body you use the **article**, not the possessive: **se rascó la cabeza**, **cruzó los brazos**.
b2.f0.texto: Lie down on the mat and keep still for a minute.
b2.f4.texto: Yawning is normal when the body relaxes.
b2.f5.texto: I sweat a lot in this posture.
b2.f6.texto: The teacher's cat has just sneezed.
b2.f7.texto: After the class you can stroke the cat.
b4.texto:
**Movement**: reflexive verb. **Se tumbó**, **me agaché**, **se puso de rodillas**.

**Result**: **estar** + participle. **Estaba tumbado**, **estoy agachada**. The participle agrees with who does it.

**Quedarse** + adjective gives the result of a change: **me quedé quieto**, **se quedaron quietas**.

**Parts of the body** take the article, not the possessive: **se rasca la cabeza**, **cruzó los brazos**.
b4.e0.texto: He bent down to pick up the keys.
b4.e1.texto: She lay on the sofa for an hour.
b4.e2.texto: The children kept still on seeing the cat.
b5.f0.texto: My grandfather has a broad forehead and white eyebrows that fall over his eyes.
b5.f1.texto: The wrinkles on his cheeks move like waves when he smiles.
b5.f2.texto: A short, rough beard covers his chin.
b5.f3.texto: His small eyes shine beneath long, dark eyelashes.
b5.f4.texto: When he bends down to tie his shoes, his back creaks like an old door.
b5.f5.texto: When he talks, he moves his hands as if he were drawing each word in the air.
b5.f6.texto: He scratches his head when he doubts and turns serious when he remembers.
b5.f7.texto: Sometimes he yawns without making a sound and closes his eyes for a moment.
b5.f8.texto: When my cat lies down on his knees, he strokes her without looking at her.
b5.f9.texto: His whole body is an open book that tells his entire life.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the reflexive verb tells the movement of lying down.
b6.o1.refuerzo: That is the result: he was already lying down and did not move.
b6.o2: Estuvo mucho tiempo en el sofá
b6.o2.refuerzo: It says nothing about the movement, only where he was.
b6.pregunta: Which sentence tells the movement of lying down?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: with the body you use the article, and «se» already says whose it is.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It sounds natural in English, but in Spanish the body takes the article.
b7.o2.refuerzo: With «una» it would sound like just any head. It is his own: «la».
b8.frase: Se agachó para recoger las llaves
b8.traduccion: He bent down to pick up the keys
b9.o0.refuerzo: That is it: we open our mouth wide when we are sleepy.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Estornudar is blowing air out of the nose; it has nothing to do with sleep.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Sudar is giving off sweat, more from heat or effort.
b9.pregunta: What does the body do when you are very sleepy?
b10.o0.refuerzo: It is singular; «los niños» needs a plural.
b10.o2.refuerzo: It is feminine; «los niños» is masculine.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: acariciar is touching softly and affectionately.
b12.o1.refuerzo: It is a reflexive verb: you scratch yourself, not the cat.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Agacharse is bending the body down; it is not touching the cat.
b12.pregunta: What do you do to touch a cat gently?
p.tumbaos.consejo: Imperative for «vosotros»: «tumbad» plus «os» gives «tumbaos», dropping the «d».
p.esterilla.consejo: The «ll» sounds like «y». It is the thin mat used for yoga or the beach.
p.quietos.consejo: It is the masculine plural of «quieto». It goes with «quedarse»: «quedaos quietos».
p.pica.consejo: «Me pica» works like «gustar»: what itches is the subject, as in «me pica la ceja».
p.rasques.consejo: «No te rasques» is a negative order. The «c» becomes «qu» to keep the «k» sound.
p.normal.consejo: It is the same for masculine and feminine: «un día normal», «una situación normal».
p.relaja.consejo: The «j» sounds like a strong h. «Relajarse» is becoming calm.
p.sudo.consejo: It is the «yo» form of «sudar»; regular verbs in «-ar» end in «-o» here.
p.acaba.consejo: «Acabar de» + infinitive says something happened a moment ago: «acaba de salir».
p.podéis.consejo: It is the «vosotros» form of «poder». It is used in Spain; in Latin America: «pueden».
p.gato.consejo: If it is female you say «gata»; «el gato» is also used in general.
p.agachó.consejo: The accent shows the stress falls on the last syllable: «agachó».
p.recoger.consejo: The «g» before «e» sounds like a strong j: «re-ko-HER».
p.estuvo.consejo: Irregular past of «estar»: «estuve», «estuvo». It is written with «v».
p.tumbada.consejo: It is the participle of «tumbarse» and agrees: «tumbado», «tumbada».
p.quedaron.consejo: The «qu» sounds «k» and the «u» is silent: «ke-DA-ron».
p.abuelo.consejo: «Abuela» is the woman. «Los abuelos» are both together.
p.cejas.consejo: Plural of «ceja». The «c» sounds «th» and the «j» like a strong h.
p.caen.consejo: In «ellos» it is «caen»: two strong vowels, in different syllables, «KA-en».
p.áspera.consejo: The accent marks the first syllable: «ÁS-pe-ra». The masculine is «áspero».
p.largas.consejo: It agrees with «pestañas»: feminine plural. The masculine is «largos».
p.agacha.consejo: «Se agacha» is the present: he gets down low. The «ch» sounds as in «chocolate».
p.atarse.consejo: «Atar» plus «se»: «atarse los zapatos» is tying your own shoes.
p.dibujara.consejo: This subjunctive form follows «como si»: «como si dibujara».
p.rasca.consejo: «Se rasca» is the present. The initial «r» rolls strongly.
p.bosteza.consejo: It is the present of «bostezar». The «z» sounds «th» and is written «z» before «a».
p.instante.consejo: It is a very short time: «un instante». It is masculine.
p.tumba.consejo: «Se tumba» is the present: it lies down. The «b» and «v» sound the same.
p.mirarla.consejo: «Mirar» plus «la»: the pronoun attaches to the infinitive and means «mirar a ella».
p.entero.consejo: It agrees: «entero», «entera». «Su cuerpo entero» is all of his body.
p.tumbó.consejo: The accent marks the last syllable: «tumbó». It is the past.
p.rascó.consejo: Past of «rascar»: the accent marks the last syllable.
p.cabeza.consejo: The «z» sounds «th» in Spain. With the body you use the article: «la cabeza».
